title: Horizon and Vector
premise: Wendell Whitlock has spent eleven years running cargo along the Silence Corridor, the trade lane severed by a war between the Meridian Compact and the Vessel States — and every jump, he passes the cryo-hold where his own backups sleep, copies made before an accident he cannot remember. When a ghost ship that never flew appears on his scopes carrying a manifest with his dead brother's name, Wendell discovers both governments have been hiding the war's true origin: a first-strike ordered using his stolen pre-accident memories as the decryption key. Pursued by Compact intelligence and a Vessel State defector who may be a copy of someone he loved, Wendell must choose between delivering the truth that ends the war and protecting the fragile identity of the man he has become. In the end he broadcasts the message himself, erasing his backups to keep it from being weaponized, and the war ends — but only one Wendell Whitlock walks out of it, finally whole because he chose to be singular.
about_author: Isandro Halloran is a former merchant marine radio officer who writes science fiction about people who work for a living among the stars. He lives in a coastal town where the fog does most of the talking.

chapters.title: The Long Quiet
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. On the run between Halcyon Reach and Coldwater, Wendell navigates the Silence Corridor, trading pleasantries with customs drones while avoiding the hold deck where his backups sleep in frost. Establishes his routine, his insomnia, and the ache of not remembering his own accident. Emotional beat: loneliness worn smooth into habit.

chapters.title: Manifest of a Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Docking at Coldwater Station, Wendell finds a berth assignment for the Perihelion Dawn — a vessel decommissioned nine years ago — listing W. Whitlock Jr. as navigator. His brother died in the war's first year. He goes to the berth and finds the ship real, cold, and waiting for him. Beat: dread sharpening into compulsion.

chapters.title: Frost on the Glass
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Aboard the Perihelion Dawn, Wendell finds a sealed courier case keyed to his biometrics and a log entry in his brother's voice: 'If you're reading this, they woke the wrong one.' Before he can open the case, station security storms the dock. He escapes with the case and burns his mooring fees behind him. Beat: flight, adrenaline, guilt.

chapters.title: What the Backups Dream
chapters.summary: POV Sefa Ilyin, a Compact intelligence analyst aboard the hunter ship Verity. She reviews Wendell's file: the accident, the memory gap, the three backups made in the year before it. Her superior orders him taken alive — specifically his hippocampal pattern. Sefa begins to suspect why. Beat: cold procedure hiding unease.

chapters.title: The Defector at Drift Nine
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. At a smuggler waypoint, a woman named Asha Corvane intercepts him claiming to be a Vessel State archivist who knows what's in the case. She is charming, competent, and wrong in small ways — she remembers a version of Wendell from before the accident. He doesn't trust her; he needs her. Beat: wary alliance.

chapters.title: Decryption Key
chapters.summary: POV Asha. In the Perihelion Dawn's cabin, they open the courier case: a data-spike containing proof the war began with a false-flag strike authorized using stolen memories — Wendell's memories, copied during a routine medical scan. His brother found out and was silenced. Beat: vertigo; the self becomes evidence.

chapters.title: Verdict of the Verity
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. The Verity corners them at Drift Nine; Sefa boards under truce and offers Wendell asylum in exchange for the spike. Asha counters with the truth of Sefa's own orders. Sefa stalls her captain, buying Wendell an escape window — and marking herself a traitor. Beat: conscience over career.

chapters.title: Three of Me
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Hiding in a comet-shielded yard, Wendell confronts the hold question directly: if his memories are the key, then so are his backups'. Whoever wakes them owns the war's origin story. He begins drafting a plan to reach the backup vault at Meridian Prime before either government does. Beat: resolve forming from fear.

chapters.title: The Route No One Speaks Of
chapters.summary: POV Asha. Asha plots a forbidden course through the Graveyard Belt, revealing more of herself than intended — she navigates it like a native. Wendell realizes she's flown it in a body that isn't hers, or a life that isn't hers. Confrontation deferred by a Compact patrol sweep. Beat: intimacy built on concealment.

chapters.title: Graveyard Transit
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. The transit sequence: derelict warships, frozen dead, a near-collision that only Wendell's instinct saves. In the quiet after, Asha admits she is a reprinted consciousness — the original Asha Corvane died delivering this same message. Wendell must decide whether a copy can be trusted with his life. Beat: grief and grace.

chapters.title: Sefa's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Branded a deserter, Sefa uses her analyst access to trace the false-flag order up the chain to Compact First Minister Oyelaran — and finds Vessel State co-signatures. Both sides built the lie together. She transmits her findings to Wendell on an open channel, knowing it ends her old life. Beat: sacrifice as clarity.

chapters.title: Meridian Prime
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. The heart of the Compact: towers, propaganda, and the Vault where his backups sleep under military seal. Using Sefa's credentials and Asha's forged manifest, they enter as corpse-recovery contractors. Wendell stands outside the vault door hearing his own heartbeat twice — once in his chest, once on the monitor inside. Beat: confrontation with the self.

chapters.title: The Man in the Tank
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Inside, Wendell faces Backup Two — awake, decanted early by vault technicians who mistake him for the original. The backup believes he is Wendell Whitlock, husband, veteran, loyal Compact citizen. Their conversation is a mirror held too close. Beat: identity as argument, not fact.

chapters.title: Oyelaran's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Arrested but not executed, Sefa is brought before First Minister Oyelaran, who reveals the endgame: wake the backups, decrypt the archive, control the narrative forever — and offer Wendell a pardon to play along. Sefa pretends to accept, becoming a double agent. Beat: chess in a gilded room.

chapters.title: Brother's Voice
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. The full message plays: his brother's recording names the joint conspiracy and carries the authentication codes to broadcast it on every fleet channel simultaneously. But broadcasting requires the vault's uplink — and the backup, hearing everything, must choose which of them is real enough to matter. Beat: the two Wendells align against the world.

chapters.title: Siege of the Vault
chapters.summary: POV Asha. Compact forces breach the vault; Asha holds the uplink room alone, reliving fragments of her original death as the corridors fill with gas and gunfire. Sefa arrives at the last moment wearing ministerial authority, freezing the assault. Beat: courage without certainty of survival.

chapters.title: Which One Lives
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. With the uplink armed, the cost surfaces: the broadcast protocol requires purging all copies of the key — including the backups in the tanks, including any part of him that could ever be duplicated again. The backup volunteers first: 'You've lived longer. Make it count.' Beat: the book's moral summit.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Wendell sends the message across every channel in human space — the false flag, the signatures, the names. Fleet channels go silent, then erupt. Oyelaran's authority collapses mid-broadcast; Vessel State hardliners move to seize the vacuum. The war could end or metastasize, and no one controls which. Beat: release and terror at once.

chapters.title: The Long Night After
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Ceasefire talks convene on neutral Coldwater Station, brokered by officers like Sefa who chose truth over service. She testifies, is pardoned, and refuses reinstatement. Asha's transmission logs become the war's official first draft of history. Beat: exhaustion transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Perihelion
chapters.summary: POV Asha. The Perihelion Dawn is scuttled with full honors, its dead brother's mission complete. Asha, legally nonexistent, receives a new identity from the very institutions that erased her original — and chooses to keep the borrowed name anyway. Beat: authorship of the self.

chapters.title: Horizon and Vector
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Months later, Wendell runs a new route on a rebuilt corridor, the hold empty by his own choice — no backups, no duplicates, one irrepeatable life. He visits his brother's memorial and finally remembers the accident without flinching: it was ordinary, survivable, human. Beat: peace earned, not granted.

chapters.title: First Light on the Corridor
chapters.summary: POV Wendell, closing frame mirroring chapter one. The same run, the same stars — but ships speak to each other now, and a passenger asks the navigator how he sleeps so well. Wendell looks back at the empty hold and answers honestly. Final beat: the future as something navigated, not repeated.
